findings.title: README is too short
findings.description: Very short READMEs typically miss installation, usage, and contribution context.
findings.recommendation: Expand the README with sections for setup, usage, and examples.

findings.title: No lockfile detected
findings.description: A lockfile pins exact dependency versions for reproducible installs.

recommendations.title: Expand the README
recommendations.rationale: Expand the README with sections for setup, usage, and examples.

recommendations.title: Re-engage maintenance signals
recommendations.rationale: Triage the open queue, ship a small maintenance release, and update topics, description, and homepage.

recommendations.title: Polish the developer onboarding flow
recommendations.rationale: An .env.example, a Makefile or Dockerfile, and clean package.json scripts shorten time-to-first-contribution.

recommendations.title: Reorganize files into clear top-level directories
recommendations.rationale: Move source, scripts, and configs out of the root into src/, scripts/, and config/.

recommendations.title: Tighten the security baseline
recommendations.rationale: If SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS, Dependabot, or a CodeQL workflow are missing, add the ones that are not yet present.

recommendations.title: Add or expand the GitHub Actions workflow
recommendations.rationale: Even a minimal Actions workflow that runs build + test + lint on each PR makes regressions visible early.

onboarding.title: Install dependencies

onboarding.title: Start the dev workflow
onboarding.rationale: Most JS/TS projects expose "dev"; check package.json scripts for the actual entry points if unsure.

onboarding.title: Run the test suite before any change
onboarding.rationale: Tests were detected in the tree even though no CI workflow was found.

onboarding.title: Read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a PR

onboarding.title: Skim the Code of Conduct
onboarding.rationale: Standard for community projects; read once so PR conversations stay productive.

story.heading: What this repository appears to be
story.body: "Sample audit fixture used to demonstrate export formats.". This is a TypeScript-based project using React running on Node.js. 1,234 stars place it firmly in the well-known tier. Lifetime growth averages around 101.4 stars per month.

story.heading: Project age and momentum
story.body: An established project at over a year old — long enough for patterns and a contributor base to settle in.

story.heading: Stack and tooling
story.body: Primary language is TypeScript at 80% of bytes. A second language carries non-trivial weight, hinting at native bindings, build tooling, or a multi-target setup.

story.heading: How alive it is
story.body: Push activity is fresh — last commit landed 7 days ago. Recent commits arrive in bursts of multiple per day (avg 1d apart). 2 distinct authors appear in the recent commit window. No tagged releases were detected. Open-issue volume looks well-managed (1 open, 0 PRs).

story.heading: Where it shines and where it slips
story.body: On the strong side: a working CI pipeline. Where it loses points: code-quality coverage is incomplete; documentation has gaps; security signals are uneven; structure could be tighter.

story.heading: What the README tells you
story.body: The README is roughly 11 words long across 3 headings. Detected sections: Sample · Installation · Usage. That is short — most readers need 300+ words to evaluate a project.

story.heading: Best next steps
story.body: The fastest score gains come from maintenance. After that, ecosystem & dependencies and developer experience would compound the improvement. Each of these has at least one finding below with a concrete action.
